purpose: Repair exactly the information loss isolated by v7.1 on the important subclass of orbit-rigid C4 interaction bundles. Instead of existentially forgetting the relative S3 gauge, retain its unique value as a function of the two orbit labels. Then global component gauges can be eliminated without 6^k enumeration: a fixed orbit assignment is gauge-realizable iff the induced relative gains have trivial holonomy on a fundamental cycle basis.

bundle_definition.ports: Each smooth complementary C4 has labelled ports 0,1,2,3 in Hamiltonian occurrence order.
bundle_definition.bundle: For two quotient components X,Y, B_XY is the set of Hamiltonian port pairs (p,q) joining X-port p to Y-port q.
bundle_definition.relative_gain: Orient X->Y and put h_XY=g_Y^{-1} composed with g_X in S3. For orbit pair (a,b), define S_B(a,b)={h in S3 : h(T_a[p]) != T_b[q] for every (p,q) in B}.
bundle_definition.orbit_rigid: B is orbit-rigid iff every nonempty S_B(a,b) is a singleton. Then write A_B={(a,b):S_B(a,b) nonempty} and h_B(a,b) for the unique member.

main_theorem.name: RIGID_RELATIVE_GAINS_ELIMINATE_TO_FUNDAMENTAL_HOLONOMY
main_theorem.statement: Let Q be a connected C4 quotient interaction multigraph in which every component-pair bundle is orbit-rigid. Fix orbit labels tau_X satisfying (tau_X,tau_Y) in A_B on every oriented quotient edge/bundle. Then global gauges {g_X in S3} satisfying every original Hamiltonian inequality exist iff the unique gains h_XY=h_B(tau_X,tau_Y) have trivial product around every cycle of Q. It suffices to check one fundamental cycle basis from any spanning tree.
proof: Necessity: if h_XY=g_Y^{-1}g_X, composition telescopes around every directed closed walk, so the cycle product is the identity.

Sufficiency: choose one root gauge arbitrarily, for example identity. On a spanning tree T, use each singleton relation h_XY=g_Y^{-1}g_X to determine the child gauge uniquely from its parent. This assigns exactly one gauge to every quotient vertex.

For a non-tree edge XY, the assigned endpoint gauges satisfy that bundle iff their induced relative gain equals its unique h_B(tau_X,tau_Y). This equality is exactly the identity of the fundamental cycle formed by XY plus the T-path between X and Y.
Therefore all non-tree edges are satisfied iff all fundamental-cycle holonomies are trivial. No gauge branching is required.
main_theorem.complexity_for_fixed_tau: Build a spanning forest, propagate gauges, and check all non-tree edges in O(|V(Q)|+|E(Q)|) group operations. S3 operations are constant-time.
main_theorem.witness_reconstruction: Once tau passes the holonomy test, the propagated gauges reconstruct every C4 vertex colour in linear time.

symbolic_compilation.input: An all-rigid quotient Q with orbit labels still unknown.
symbolic_compilation.output: Keep only the 3-state variables tau_X, the binary admissibility relations A_B, and for each fundamental cycle a compact S3 word constraint requiring the product of the corresponding h_B(tau_X,tau_Y) terms (or inverses when traversed backwards) to equal identity.
symbolic_compilation.size: A spanning tree has |V|-1 edges and at most |E|-|V|+1 fundamental cycles. Storing each cycle as references to quotient edges is polynomial size; a naive explicit representation is O(|V||E|), and shared path/tree representations can be smaller.
symbolic_compilation.exactness: For every tau assignment, the compiled instance accepts exactly when some global gauge assignment exists. Thus the S3 gauge variables are eliminated exactly on the all-rigid subclass without enumerating 6^|V| states.
symbolic_compilation.firewall: This compilation alone is not a polynomial decision algorithm for the remaining tau variables; the resulting 3-state orbit-plus-holonomy CSP may still be hard.

v7_1_control_repair.fact: All three component-pair bundles in the v7.1 twelve-vertex smooth-C4 control are orbit-rigid: every accepted orbit pair has exactly one allowed relative S3 gain.
v7_1_control_repair.cycle_check: For orientation 0->1->2 and direct 0->2, consistency requires h02 = h12 composed with h01. The left side is permutation index 4 while the right side is index 3, so the holonomy check rejects the pairwise false positive immediately.
v7_1_control_repair.meaning: v7.1 did not require retaining three independent 6-state gauges on this control. The exact missing bit is the nontrivial product of the unique relative gains around the quotient triangle.

finite_local_catalog.scope: Exhaust every simple C4-to-C4 port bundle B subseteq {0,1,2,3}^2 with no port used more than twice inside that bundle, as required by Hamiltonian degree two at each original vertex.
finite_local_catalog.interpretation: Rigidity is a substantial exact local class starting at three cross-edges, but it is not universal. The catalog is only a finite local classification; it makes no distributional claim about hard instances.

positive: Exact linear-time gauge reconstruction/checking for any fixed orbit assignment on an all-rigid quotient.
Exact polynomial-size elimination of all component S3 gauges into orbit admissibility plus cycle holonomy constraints on the all-rigid subclass.
A constant-time recognizer/table for whether any C4 port bundle is orbit-rigid and, when it is, for its unique gain function h_B.
A direct repair of the v7.1 pairwise false positive without restoring exponential gauge enumeration.
not_solved: Choosing the tau orbit labels globally in polynomial time on arbitrary rigid quotients.
Non-rigid bundles with two, three, or four allowed relative gains.
The full smooth fixed-inner-cycle NP-hard source.

next_target.name: E8_C4_RIGID_ORBIT_HOLONOMY_CSP_POLYMORPHISM_OR_NONRIGID_CORE_V7_3
next_target.directive: Separate the quotient into rigid and non-rigid bundles. First classify the finite binary orbit relations A_B and gain functions h_B of all rigid bundle symmetry types and test whether the resulting 3-state fundamental-holonomy CSP has a Maltsev/affine/group polymorphism or already contains a known hard finite-domain relation. In parallel contract any full-state functional/bijective rigid edges. Only then attack non-rigid gain-set atoms. Mandatory controls: v7.1 holonomy triangle, v6.8 balanced-mutation pair, v7.0 essentially-6 graph, and the smooth Hamiltonian source.
